text: The evaluation framework operates within an isolated Mahimahi network namespace to ensure synchronized, reproducible emulation.
Inside this namespace, a kernel TCP/IP stack manages multiple congestion control algorithms alongside standard socket interfaces.
On the sender side, servers transmit network traffic guided by link traces.
Packets from each sender enter the Mahimahi namespace via dedicated ingress TUN interfaces.
Chained user-space shells dynamically emulate path impairments, including packet loss and variable delay.
Traffic is concurrently processed by the kernel stack across baseline reference controllers, including NewReno, Cubic, and BBR.
Packets then exit through egress TUN interfaces to reach the receiving clients.
Meanwhile, the learned Sage controller receives transport observations from the socket and executes its policy actions in real time.
A Control Block coordinates the user-space shells by updating downlink and uplink bandwidth, loss, and delay parameters.
Finally, ReGuard aggregates telemetry, action histories, and rewards across Sage and heuristic baselines to uncover worst-case failure scenarios.
